request.spec:
Add an audit viewer to the screen: a filter entry, a show button and a list of lines. With the
filter blank it lists every audit line of this sheet exactly as the file holds it, newest first.
With a name in the filter it lists only the lines about that person: those carrying name=<the
name> or person=<the name>, compared as names are compared (case and surrounding spaces ignored).
The viewer reads what the file holds; it is not a second record.

agent.result_text:
I added the audit viewer, and all 4 acceptance tests pass on `bin/e2e`.

**What you see:** a new panel near the bottom of the sheet screen with a person filter (`audit-filter`), a Show button (`audit-show`) and the list of lines (`audit-line`).
- **Blank filter:** pressing Show lists every audit line for this sheet, newest first, exactly as the file holds it.
- **Name in the filter:** only lines carrying `name=<the name>` or `person=<the name>` are listed. Case and surrounding spaces are ignored, so `" ada "` finds Ada's lines.
- The old list clears when Show is pressed again, so two presses with the same result can still be told apart.

**How it works:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit?name=…`, reads the audit file directly through a new `lines(sheetId, name)` method on the existing `Audit` service. Nothing is stored in a second place, and viewing writes nothing to the file.

A name containing spaces (e.g. `name=Ada Lovelace`) is read up to the next `key=` field. None of the tests use such a name.

**Files changed:**
- `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/Audit.java` (added `lines`)
- `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/auditview/RespondWithAuditLines.java` (new)
- `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit.GET.yml` (new)
- `src/main/frontend/features/auditView/auditView.slot.tsx` (new)
